evidence.locator: Local commands; registry; credentials; permissions; checkpoints

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/outside-agents.md
evidence.locator: Read-only default; approved scopes; host scripts; revoke
evidence.finding: OAuth HTTP MCP supports project and thread read/start/send/stop and provider discovery. Read-only is default; approved modes cap operations. evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/permission-modes.md
evidence.locator: Initial default; child requests; provider differences
evidence.finding: New threads initially use Full access, with user and project overrides. Supervised asks for command and edit approval, Auto-accept edits covers edits, and Auto uses a provider reviewer where available. Child approvals appear in the parent; provider enforcement differs.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/project-settings.md
evidence.locator: Scheduled tasks; Webhooks; scopes and cleanup
evidence.finding: Environment-owned tasks support once, recurrence and webhooks. Webhooks offer signatures, filters, seven-day dedupe and restart-persistent coalescing. Optional Connect buffering holds offline requests for up to 24 hours; cleanup controls are separate and default off.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: apps/web/src/components/chat/ProposedPlanCard.tsx
evidence.locator: Plan actions: copy, download Markdown, save workspace; TimelineAssistantRows integration
evidence.finding: The rendered plan card exposes Markdown, copy, download and workspace save guarded by filesystem-write permission. The thread timeline renders these artifacts. This does not establish a maintained spec or approval workflow.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/orchestration-v2/orchestrator-mcp-server.md
evidence.locator: Purpose; provider injection; delegate_task; task_status; follow-ups; scheduled tasks
evidence.finding: T3 MCP delegates child threads across compatible providers with roles, models, scoped credentials, idempotency keys and durable task results. Children receive the supplied task and optional role without parent history. Follow-ups preserve the published result and run as a fresh task.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/orchestrator/tools.ts
evidence.finding: The stable OrchestratorToolkit registers delegation, status, cancellation, thread and schedule tools, and McpHttpServer registers that toolkit. Tool descriptions expose isolated worktrees and model/role choices, connecting the contract to the shipped path.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/thread-sidebar.md
evidence.locator: Inspect agent work; Resume at reset; side chats; thread metadata
evidence.finding: Threads support manual Resume and optional reset-time continuation. Parent conversations show child questions and approvals. Side chats can bring context back; saved thread metadata and message search are documented.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/providers-pi.md
evidence.finding: Pi approval modes apply through a blocking tool hook, explicitly not an OS sandbox. Trusted extension code retains the Pi trust boundary. T3 delegate_task creates durable child threads distinct from an installed native subagent extension.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/portable-handoffs.md
evidence.locator: Context selection; omitted history retrieval; limits
evidence.finding: Portable handoff selects bounded original and recent messages and results, excluding reasoning, tool state and attachments. References allow retrieving omitted saved history. A full window can start a fresh provider conversation; the new request is never shortened.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/thread-migration.md
evidence.finding: V1 migration copies SQLite and imports messages, attachments and settings but not the old live process, run/checkpoint, approval or plan state. Continuation starts a fresh provider session with bounded history. No whole-thread export command exists; a stopped userdata backup is the documented recovery path.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/providers-opencode.md
evidence.finding: After lost connection, another prompt reconnects to the same OpenCode session. Restricted modes require approval for environment files. Allow for workspace affects matching requests across sessions; denial does not end the whole turn.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/terminal.md
evidence.finding: The environment server retains at most 5,000 lines and 8 MiB of terminal scrollback, dropping oldest output at either limit. Reconnect and restored history share those bounds; retained output can be copied.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/telemetry.md
evidence.locator: Product events; mobile crash report; own OTLP receiver
evidence.finding: Server product events exclude prompts, responses, files and authentication data. Mobile crash reports can include handled error values and have an opt-out. Operators can export traces, metrics and logs to their own OTLP receivers; server telemetry and managed-policy controls remain separate.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/guest-links.md
evidence.locator: Beta setup; Send/Dismiss; What the guest sees; attachments
evidence.finding: Optional beta links require Labs and T3 Connect, authorize one browser for 24 hours and stream recent/live thread history. Guest text and files wait for the owner to Send or Dismiss. Guests lack model, file, rewind and provider-answer authority; ending sharing revokes access.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/managed-policy.md
evidence.locator: OS rollout; enforcement; capability/provider permission caps
evidence.finding: Administrators deploy JSON, macOS device profiles or Windows Group Policy. The server enforces locked settings and limits for all clients, rejects invalid policies and reloads only on restart. This is machine management, not organization SSO or SCIM.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/source-control.md
evidence.locator: PR review and mobile; Review guides; viewed marks; watchers; stacks
evidence.finding: Stable mobile PR review supports diffs and draft comments. Optional beta guides tour every changed file, group mechanical changes and hide stale excerpts. Server-retained viewed marks show Changed after pushes. Shared PR polling wakes agents for checks, reviews and conflicts; GitHub stack actions are available.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: remote access
evidence.locator: T3 Connect, scripts, LAN pairing and remote machines
evidence.finding: Agents execute on a user-owned machine running the environment; clients connect over T3 Connect, private pairing or SSH. The host must remain running and reachable. A separate remote host continues work when the laptop client disconnects.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/background-service.md
evidence.locator: Manage the service; Platform support; Troubleshooting
evidence.finding: On Linux and macOS t3 service install runs T3 Code as a per-user service. Linux setup enables lingering so it keeps running after logout; the macOS service stops at logout; Windows background services are not supported.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/keybindings.md
evidence.locator: Composer controls; Copy pull request references; Find in a diff; Commands with special behavior
evidence.finding: Shortcuts are customised in Settings > Keybindings on web and desktop. thread.stop interrupts the running turn and has no default shortcut. mod+f searches a Diff panel or pull request Code tab diff (not configurable); mod+shift+c and mod+shift+k copy a PR URL or number.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/mobile-notifications.md
evidence.finding: With T3 Connect and Device Notifications enabled, phones get alerts when an agent finishes, fails, needs approval or asks for input. Background delivery requires T3 Connect; the app need not keep a connection to the environment.

evidence.finding: The feature request for on-demand cloud task environments was converted from issue #14793 to an open Ideas discussion on 11 October 2026. It is a request, not a shipped capability.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/updating.md
evidence.finding: Server updates can interrupt active agents and terminal commands; saved threads, settings and project files remain. Settings > Maintenance > Continue threads after restarts is on by default and resumes supported active threads after an update, crash or machine restart; threads without saved provider resume state need a new message, and after three automatic resumes in a row a thread waits for the user.

evidence.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/internals/overview.md
evidence.finding: Checkpoints use hidden Git refs to capture workspace state without adding commits to the user's branch. A provider that cannot roll back its conversation must reject a revert before the filesystem changes.

integration_owner.answer: T3 owns the environment MCP/orchestration endpoint and generic ACP adapter; external agents own their tool implementations, credentials and native config.

webhooks.answer: On webhook scheduled tasks accept external requests with configurable signature checks, filters, duplicate keys and coalescing; public URLs require T3 Connect. No outbound webhook contract is claimed.

roles.answer: delegate_task accepts an implementation, research, review, design, test or general role instruction for a T3-owned child thread.

model_harness_effort.answer: Delegation selects a compatible provider instance and advertised model, inheriting parent choices when omitted. Independent reasoning-effort controls depend on the provider.

messages.answer: Thread tools send or steer follow-ups and read incremental thread history. Child questions and results can notify the parent.

results_return.answer: Read the durable result with task_status or wait for it. A wait timeout leaves the child running; known child work must finish before result_available.

cross_harness.answer: T3-owned delegation can choose a different compatible provider instance/model rather than only a native harness child.

orchestration_owner.answer: T3 MCP and V2 child-thread lifecycle own delegation and durable results; this is distinct from provider-native subagents.

activation.answer: Compatible provider sessions receive the app-owned MCP endpoint with session credential; active parent-run authority is required for delegation.

authentication.answer: Credentials are scoped to the environment, parent thread, provider instance and provider session. They expire and revoke with session lifecycle; handlers require orchestration capability.

retained_results.answer: A task published result/summary remains stable after terminal completion; later followups do not rewrite it.

followup.answer: Send to childThreadId to continue its conversation. After the original task completes, a follow-up becomes a fresh task without rewriting the published result.

invocation.answer: The model calls delegate_task with a prompt, optional role and target. task_status, task_cancel and wait inspect or control the execution.

schedules.answer: Tasks support recurring intervals or fixed times and a one-time date and time, on the selected environment server.

events.answer: Webhook tasks accept external requests with optional signatures, filters and deduplication. PR watchers also wake agents on changed checks, comments or conflicts.

recurring_tasks.answer: Scheduled prompts can post into an existing thread or start a fresh thread per run. Users can edit, pause, resume or delete schedules.

completion_conditions.answer: Delegated task results wait for known child work to finish. A scheduled dispatch is not documented as acceptance of the requested business outcome.

scheduler_location.answer: The chosen environment owns app scheduler execution even without an active turn. Fixed-time recurrence uses its time zone.

overlaps.answer: Webhook keys suppress duplicate requests for seven days; coalescing combines a burst into its latest payload and survives restart. General limits on overlapping recurring runs remain unestablished.

retries.answer: One-time runs missed while offline execute when the environment returns. Webhook senders normally redeliver errors; optional T3 Connect buffering lasts up to 24 hours and can skip old requests.

resume.answer: Resume in an empty composer continues a limited or interrupted turn. Resume at reset schedules continuation when the provider supplies a reset time.

visible_errors.answer: Limited threads retain provider explanation; failed runs/input/approvals return attention to the active list and child requests surface to the parent.

parent_child.answer: Agents view and subagent conversation cards expose delegated child work and parent links on web/desktop/mobile. A dependency/workload fleet fixture was not run.

history.answer: Thread search includes saved message text and references; task_status preserves terminal child results. A multi-day fleet history scenario was not run.

natural_language.answer: An agent can use T3 MCP tools to delegate a described prompt and role or schedule recurring work; no complete evolving-epic fixture was run.

live_roles.answer: Each delegated task can choose a role, provider and model. Editing the role of a running child in place is not established.

retained_relationships.answer: Durable tasks keep their parent, child thread and run IDs, and published result, including finalization after server restart.

discoverability.answer: orchestrator_capabilities lists compatible providers/models and missing availability/auth constraints; this is agent tool discovery, not a measured human discoverability study.

os_sandbox.answer: The Pi approval hook is explicitly not an OS sandbox. Generic ACP agents enforce their own native sandbox and rules; no universal T3 process sandbox is established.

filesystem.answer: Threads can share a checkout or use separate worktrees. File rewind is refused when another thread or session uses an overlapping directory. This protects against overwriting work, rather than providing general filesystem confinement.

process.answer: Registry tools/processes run under the agent native policy; for most registry agents T3 displays native terminal output but does not run/stop those terminals.

security_boundary.answer: Pi hook governs tool calls only and native ACP agents own sandbox policy. Worktrees are file separation, not a claimed universal command security boundary.

code_separation.answer: Worktrees separate branch files. Rewind refuses shared or overlapping directories to avoid erasing another session’s changes.

transcript_reload.answer: V1 migration imports saved messages and attachments, but does not recreate old live runs, checkpoints, approvals or plan artifacts.

process_reconnect.answer: After an OpenCode connection is lost, the next prompt reconnects to the same native session. Recovery of all external processes across a host crash is not established.

task_resume.answer: Interrupted or limited turns can resume manually or at a reported reset time. Portable restart can open a fresh provider conversation using bounded saved history.

state_reconstruction.answer: Migration retains title, project, model, modes, branch, archive, snooze, pin and linked PR state plus messages. It does not recreate the live provider process or old tool, approval and checkpoint state.

context_loss.answer: Portable handoff excludes outgoing reasoning, tool state and attachments; omitted saved messages remain retrievable. Migration does not convert old tool, approval or plan history.

duplicate_actions.answer: Delegation retry keys provide stable identities and result finalization is idempotent. Thread launch has no retry key, so callers should inspect after a lost response. Webhook deduplication is optional.

manual_repair.answer: If migrated history appears incomplete, preserve a stopped userdata backup and inspect legacy SQLite read-only. Repeat essential constraints before continuing.

services.answer: Thread details list servers started by its terminals or Claude, including ports. Open them in the browser or stop the server without ending the agent. Automatic service sharing and port allocation are unestablished.

ports.answer: The thread details card lists detected server ports. Stop requires terminal access and is unavailable on Windows. Deterministic per-workspace port allocation is unestablished.

retries.answer: Limit stops can schedule Resume at reset and hold queued messages; overdue continuations are recovered. Missing reset times require manual Resume. This is not a general error retry policy.

enforcement.answer: Managed policy caps provider, client and permission capabilities. Product-wide spend, token and time budget enforcement is not established; native provider quotas remain separate.

logs.answer: The server retains bounded terminal output. Settings → Maintenance → Diagnostics can export logs to an operator’s OTLP receiver. Mobile crash diagnostics have a separate toggle.

traces.answer: Settings can export traces, metrics and logs to an operator’s OTLP receiver. Relay traces separately go to Axiom unless disabled.

failure_reasons.answer: Tool activity exposes commands, status, exit codes and output; Limited threads retain the provider explanation. No full operational-console scenario was tested.

failure_status.answer: Threads and delegated tasks expose limited, failed, cancelled and interrupted states to the UI or parent.

approval_status.answer: Pending child requests appear in the parent conversation. task_status reports a live pending approval or question without granting authority to approve it.

visibility.answer: An optional beta guest link lets one browser without an account follow recent thread history and live messages, files and tool output.

discussion.answer: Guests can send questions and files that wait for the owner to Send or Dismiss. This is moderated thread input rather than separate issue discussion.

coprompting.answer: A guest can submit instructions into the same agent thread, but every message waits for the owner Send decision; simultaneous unrestricted co-steering is not established.

ordering.answer: Guest messages appear at the end of the thread and wait for the owner to send or dismiss them. No conflicting-input ordering scenario was tested.

permissions.answer: Guests cannot change models, fork, revert, open host files or answer provider requests. The owner explicitly sends each guest prompt.

plan_restrictions.answer: Guest links are an optional Labs beta and require account-backed T3 Connect. No paid guest-plan requirement is stated.

provisioning.answer: Administrators can deploy JSON policy, macOS device profiles or Windows Group Policy for machine-wide settings and capability limits. Changes require server restart. User membership and SCIM provisioning are not established.

tool.answer: Supervised mode asks for command, file and extension-tool approvals. Read-only actions and provider enforcement differ.

secret.answer: OpenCode .env and .env.local reads need approval in restricted modes. Native credential stores remain the harness responsibility.

delivery.answer: Command, edit and child approval requests appear in the conversation or parent for approval or rejection. Guest prompts have a separate Send/Dismiss gate.

lifetime.answer: Grok can remember edits for the session. OpenCode Allow for workspace applies across sessions in that workspace; Allow once covers one request. Universal approval expiry is unestablished.

allow.answer: Conversation approval, Allow once and workspace choices let the scoped request continue, depending on the provider.

deny.answer: Reject declines a request. OpenCode denial does not end the whole turn; a Claude text reply can decline with feedback.

tunnels.answer: T3 Connect tunnels, private-network pairing and SSH expose the user’s host with scoped credentials and revocation.

enforcement.answer: Machine policy caps permitted modes, providers and clients; an invalid policy prevents startup. Provider-native controls still determine command confinement.

change_understanding.answer: Optional beta review guides tour changed files in ordered stops, with maintainer questions and mechanical changes grouped at the end. Claude or Codex writes the guide, which is stored on the server. No usability fixture ran.

request_changes.answer: Line comments remain drafts until the review is sent. Work on PR and guide questions open an agent with review context. Exact-revision acceptance enforcement is not established.

shipping_guidance.answer: PR views offer merge, auto-merge and stack actions. Finish review opens collected draft comments; no timed acceptance fixture ran.

retained_context.answer: Review guides persist for users of the server. Stale guides offer rewriting and hide mismatched excerpts; pushed files show Changed on retained viewed marks.

narrow_screen.answer: Current mobile PR views show diffs and draft comments; review guide stops provide Next and back controls. No narrow-screen usability or performance fixture ran.

configured_policy.answer: GitHub, GitLab and Azure DevOps auto-merge waits for host checks. This is external code-host policy, rather than a T3-executed test or spec gate.

failure_blocking.answer: Auto-merge waits while host checks are outstanding, and PR watchers can wake an agent after failed checks. A T3-side required-test policy is unestablished.

ci_response.answer: watch_pull_request polls every two minutes and wakes an agent for failed checks, required checks passing, other users’ reviews or comments, and conflicts. Watchers in one project share a poll; repeated non-progress news is bounded.

commit_links.answer: Supported code-host commit links open the local commit diff when available; a PR commit link otherwise opens the PR. Branch comparison can show the newest 100 commits.

retained_evidence.answer: Review guides and viewed marks persist on the server. Checkpoints, linked PR state and file history remain separate; an immutable task delivery receipt is unestablished.

summaries.answer: Optional beta review guides provide an ordered tour of all changed files. No six-task batch review fixture ran.

grouping.answer: Guides group mechanical changes at the end; linked PRs group GitHub stacks. Arbitrary issue-batch grouping is unestablished.

findings.answer: Guide stops include maintainer questions and agent follow-up routes, leaving out resolved review discussions. A structured independent finding lifecycle is unestablished.

request_changes.answer: Draft comments from the Code and Guide tabs stay collected until review submission; Work on PR or a guide question opens the relevant agent context.

dependency_queues.answer: GitHub stack merge submits the selected layer and its unmerged ancestors. Rebase stack updates bottom-up; a general issue-dependent release queue is unestablished.

next_actions.answer: Finish review opens collected draft comments. The PR view offers checkout, merge and stack actions; no high-volume acceptance fixture ran.

stale_approval_invalidation.answer: Stale guides hide mismatched excerpts and offer rewriting; pushed files show Changed. This updates review context, without establishing automatic revocation of exact-head approval.

check_deduplication.answer: PR watchers in one project share polling, with conditional GitHub reads for unchanged state. This does not deduplicate tests run by agents.

export.answer: The current guide explicitly says there is no whole-thread export command. A stopped userdata backup and read-only SQLite queries are recovery options, rather than a portable export contract.

formats.answer: Recovery copies include userdata and SQLite databases. V1 migration imports full transcripts but does not provide portable whole-thread export.

history_portability.answer: V1 migration retains messages and attachments, but omits old run, checkpoint, approval and plan records and starts a fresh provider session. Cross-provider handoff carries bounded text rather than full execution state.

code_data.answer: The FAQ says code and prompts go from the user host to the configured provider, rather than T3. Guest links expose visible thread content; optional offline webhook buffering stores request bodies outside the host for up to 24 hours.

credentials.answer: Registry agents keep native login stores. The security policy says credentials use platform-protected storage where supported; portable handoff does not transfer native credentials.

logs.answer: The server retains bounded terminal history. Product events exclude prompt, file and authentication content; separate mobile and relay diagnostics go to Axiom, while operator OTLP export is configurable.

artifacts.answer: Sent attachments stay with the thread. Unsent guest files are deleted on dismissal, ending sharing or archive; browser captures have separate configured retention.

paid_only.answer: The FAQ explicitly says there is currently no way to pay for T3 Code, which is free and open source. Provider and user-host costs remain separate.

free_scenarios.answer: Core T3 Code and T3 Connect are currently free. Connect permits three linked machines, excluding phones and browsers. Self-hosting, LAN and Tailscale remain alternatives.
